summary: A CCC-built sandstone summit building (work began 1938, finished 1941-42) with a lookout floor now used for radio gear; the museum draws visitors.

facts.design: Sandstone summit building with viewing deck, museum space, a fire lookout floor and a rotating aircraft beacon
facts.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation (Mount Diablo State Park)

access.note: The summit museum and visitor center is for visitors; the lookout floor holds radio repeater equipment and is not accessible.

visit.trail_note: Visitors head to the summit museum for the view, and the park road passes CCC-built picnic sites on the way to the summit. The sources give no current hours.

events.note: A fire on the south slope nearly destroyed a lookout station on the peak, per a July 28, 1931 newspaper excerpt; the station is not otherwise described

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1938, when CCC work began. State parks says the lookout portion was finished in 1941 and the rest in 1942. Read 1938 as the start and 1941-42 as completion.
A 1931 newspaper excerpt on a fan site describes a lookout station on the summit before the CCC building. The register does not mention an earlier station, and nothing read describes it.

resolved_conflicts.field: lookout use of the top floor
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the top floor was used by lookouts, and notes that several park rangers and books do not mention it. The account rests on one retired ranger.

notes_for_editor: The brief's note about conflicting materials is not borne out in the sources read: the register and state parks both say sandstone, and no source named another material. The brief's 1938 build date is the CCC start year; completion was 1941-42 per state parks, which is a substantive difference for the record. The 1931 lookout station comes from a newspaper excerpt reprinted on a fan site (californialookouts.weebly.com), not checked against the original paper. A mdia.org search snippet mentions Company 2932-V starting in 1938; the page was read only in part and that detail is not cited. No source read gives current hours for the summit museum, so the visit note is general.
